# Nivra 0.1.0-alpha.13 — Modelling and account-based model refresh

## Model refresh
- Resolves Windows npm Codex shims to the native Codex executable without creating a shell. Tests cover modern hoisted/nested optional packages and legacy vendor layout.
- The refresh control now fetches every page of the authenticated Codex model catalog, rather than a static list or only page one.
- Keeps provider model IDs, display names, supported reasoning levels, and timestamps. New names do not require a Nivra release.
- Refresh restarts an idle app-server to avoid its in-process catalog cache; it never interrupts an active turn. A lock protects concurrent turn startup.
- On refresh failure the previous list remains visible with an error, rather than disappearing.
- Reports installed CLI version and recommends updating versions older than 0.153.0. This does not grant account access or silently switch subscription/API billing.

## Game Development / Modelling
- Development and Modelling are separate tabs in the existing Game Development workspace. Unity and Unreal remain available.
- Start local Blender with an authenticated bridge, or connect an already open Blender without replacing its scene.
- Project-local modelling tools: inspect/create/custom meshes/transform/duplicate/delete/materials/modifiers/UVs/smooth shading/select/save/open/import/export/checkpoint/capture.
- Full-access users can run advanced bpy scripts, with an automatic scene checkpoint. This is explicitly not an OS sandbox.
- Codex dynamic tools and Claude API tools share the same Nivra chat, workspace, permissions, activity and cancellation layer.
- Blender captures can be returned as image input to the agent after the capture operation completes.
- Scene status, object search, operation results and file controls use real responses, not simulated progress.
- Last existing project-local .blend path is remembered. Unsaved Blender changes still need explicit saving.
- Scene sessions, logs, checkpoints and the modelling skill live in Nivra application data, not copied into the game repository.
- A lightweight scene poll does not launch new shells or scan toolchains repeatedly.

## Reliability and UI
- Connected the actual global Stop endpoint to chat controls, Esc and Modelling Stop. Queued operations are cancelled; Blender itself is never killed by Stop.
- Chat stays within the window with its own scroll and visible composer. Collapsed Output no longer reserves a large empty region.
- Refresh buttons have real busy states. Edits are disabled when Blender is disconnected.
- Binary .blend/.uasset/.umap files are blocked from text editing.
- Publisher validates the destination remote before repository maintenance and preserves unpublished commits, patches and untracked files in backups.

## Test scope
94 top-level Go tests + 7 subtests passed; 2 live-editor tests skipped (Blender and Unreal not installed).
6 pure Python validation tests and 2 publisher tests passed.
Chromium renderer checked at four sizes with zero script exceptions; protocol peers are explicitly test doubles.
Live Windows/WebView2, real Blender bpy operations, live OpenAI/Claude accounts and signed public deployment are not tested in this build environment.
